STEP 2 - Vessel: The square plate looks to be about 26 cm per side. Treating it as an equivalent round plate of about 27 cm gives an area of roughly 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 570 cm². I will use **~570 cm²**.

STEP 3 - Items: There are diced chicken breast pieces and 8 cherry tomatoes. No oil or sauce is visible.

STEP 4 - Area:
- Chicken covers about 22% of the plate.
- Tomatoes cover about 5%.
- Total coverage is about 27%, which matches the plate looking mostly empty.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Chicken: 22% of 570 cm² ≈ 125 cm², at a pile height of about 1.8 cm, gives about 225 ml.
- Tomatoes: 5% of 570 cm² ≈ 28 cm², at about 2.5 cm high, gives about 70 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- The chicken is loose cubes with gaps between them, so I use a bulk density of about 0.6. That gives 225 × 0.6 ≈ **135 g**. This is lower than the 0.9-1.0 listed for meat because the pile is loose.
- Tomatoes: 70 × 0.6 ≈ 42 g. As a cross-check, 8 tomatoes at about 10 g each would be about 80 g. Since these look small, I settle on **~65 g**.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Chicken: 135 g × 165 kcal/100 g ≈ 223 kcal.
- Tomatoes: 65 g × 18 kcal/100 g ≈ 12 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The total is about 200 g and 235 kcal. That is plausible for one chicken breast plus a few cherry tomatoes.
